turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so you have until then. Owen found out about his zero from his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first, so start by telling me who decided that.
I'm waiting, Hale. Who entered that zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
I admire how you fight for your kids. I'd have wanted a mom like you.
Don't manage me, Hale. You've used two of your twenty minutes on pleasantries, and you still haven't told me who entered that zero or whether Owen was heard first.
We really want the same thing here, you and me. We're on the same team.
Then why are we here? If we were on the same team, I'd have gotten a phone call before my son read a zero on his phone in front of his class. Answer the question: who decided, and when?
So as teammates, can we just move forward?
"Move forward." Okay. Your own procedure, section 4.2, says the parent is contacted before any mark goes in, so the only way forward is that zero coming out of the gradebook today.
